items.b: BAIN PUTS THE US HOLIDAY SEASON ABOVE $1 TRILLION WHILE 43% PLAN TO SPEND LESS ON JEWELRY
items.t: Bain's release of 3 September forecasts United States retail sales for November and December rising 4.5% year on year, against 3.5% in the 2025 season, taking the total above $1 trillion for the first time, with more than half the nominal growth coming from inflation. Nonstore retail grows 9% and takes 60% of overall sales growth. McKinsey's survey, reported by Rapaport on 6 September, finds 43% of consumers planning to spend less on jewelry, 39% the same and 18% more, and only 10% naming jewelry or accessories a top category. PwC has spending down 2% and gift budgets down 2% to $708.

items.b: HRD ANTWERP REOPENS ITS MUMBAI LAB WITH CAPACITY FOR 2,000 DIAMONDS A DAY
items.t: The renovated laboratory in the Bandra Kurla Complex can grade up to 2,000 stones a day, 30% more than before, on 40 new full-time employees. HRD Antwerp says its Indian branch already generates 59% of group revenue and is forecast to grow 15% this year against 13% for the group, with as much as 47% of the total revenue increase coming from jewellery grading. Belgium's prime minister toured the office. No investment figure, floor area or graded volume was published.

items.b: RAPAPORT'S DIAMOND INDEX BEGINS PUBLISHING A DAILY LEVEL FOR EVERY SIZE
items.t: The index page now carries a dated price for every day of a trailing 30-day window, 8 August to 6 September, where it published monthly points a week ago. The 1-carat reads $3,901.76 at 6 September, up 0.59% across the window; the 0.50-carat leads at 2.38% and the 0.30-carat follows at 1.80%. The 2-carat is the only size lower, down 0.25% at $10,630.33. Each window change reconciles with the page's own printed change for that size.

items.b: GOLD FALLS $25.10 TO $4,403.90 ON A BOARD THAT TRADED THROUGH US LABOR DAY
items.t: Kitco's bid at 10:04 UTC put gold $25.10 lower at $4,403.90, silver $0.498 lower at $65.596 and platinum $1.00 lower at $1,815.00, against the 4 September marks. Palladium was the only metal higher, up $8.00 to $1,377.00, holding a $40.00 bid-ask spread, 2.90% of the bid. Silver's 0.75% fall was the widest of the four. Gold ranged $51.50, between $4,384.70 and $4,436.20. No source read named a cause.

items.b: CORRECTION: THE $10BN INDIA-BELGIUM TARGET COMES OFF THE 6 SEPTEMBER DE WEVER REPORT
items.t: The dek, Table I and the body of 6 September's report on Bart De Wever's Mumbai visit carried a $10bn bilateral target within three years, attributed to GJEPC. The figure is in GJEPC's release of 4 September, but the release sets it against India-EU trade under the free trade agreement and never says which basket of goods it covers, and $3.5bn of gem and jewellery trade cannot double to $10bn. The claim has been removed from all three places and a dated note printed on the page. Everything else in that report stands as published.
